title: I work in the trades. 3 weeks ago I started building an open-world construction sim where every piece of ground is diggable. Is it worth continuing?
author: TechStandpoint
selftext:
I'm in the trades and have worked in multiple different positions in construction. I'm not a developer. About 3 weeks ago I started building an open-world construction simulator where every piece of ground is diggable, with AI doing the coding (Claude on an Ultra plan and ChatGPT on a Pro plan) and Tripo for the AI 3D models, with me directing it and correcting everything from what the real job is like.

I'm putting in multiple different machines: excavator, dozer, dump truck, hydrovac, skid steer, roller, water truck, and a mat grapple for laying access mat roads.

It's very early and rough. This is real in-game footage, not a render. Controls and digging still need a lot of work.

Honest question: would you play this? I need some motivation to keep going. Feedback welcome, good or bad.

comments.author: alanbdee
comments.body:
Its not something I'd quit your job over and mortgage your house to buy AI tokens. But that's just because the game market is getting flooded. 

I do think there is a place for games like this that are complex or somewhat realistic. Building is fun, until you hurt your back that is. If you can turn it into a game, that can be fun. It may not appeal to everyone but there is a place for it. 

I like to think of it like YouTube vs broadcast TV. When YouTube made it easy enough for anyone to make a video, people did. I think we're seeing a similar situation in games. Some games are garbage AI slop. But from that will come some real gems. 

I can't tell you that yours will be a gem or not. Because that all depends on your vision and how much time you spend fiddling with the controls to make it feel right. What I can tell you is that it will be a lot of work. It's amazing what AI can do. But it's not enough to make your idea shine. 

People out there bragging about one prompting a game are flat out wrong. That's like bragging about having sex for 30 seconds. The real work takes months to years. Are you willing to commit to that? If not, it'll end up being just another AI slop project added to the huge pile that nobody plays.

replies.author: Arctovigil
replies.body:
I think it comes down to about 3 tiers of effort invested:

1. "Guess better" by actually requiring more development time spent into the physics engine along with quickly fetched and read sources and at most using quick and easy sites or apis like OpenAlex / consensus.app or whatever such sites exist along with running a larger LLM more often for the expanded detailed work.

2. "Defensible design" exhaust effort hunting down sources that are not easily accessible until you have a defensible design at least for game engine purposes. You would be manually getting sources you can't easily get perhaps even visiting libraries and such or at least clicking through bot prevention and captchas.

3. "Serious game" you make contacts in the industry or different fields of expertise and make the game viable and vetted for serious simulations. It would become something between a toy and a tool.

More effort than 3 and you would be making a professional tool for industrial use which you might not want to do as a first project at least.

comments.author: NovaGameFR
comments.body:
Your biggest asset isn't the AI, it's that you've actually done the job. Most construction sims feel off because they're made by people who never ran a machine. A hydrovac and a mat grapple for access roads is the kind of detail only someone from the trades would add, and that's what the niche audience will notice.



I'm a web dev building a multiplayer game with Claude, and 3 weeks in is very early. Rough controls are normal at this stage. One tip that helped me keep going: pick one machine and make it feel really good before adding the next. One great excavator will hook people more than eight average ones, and it gives you a clean clip to show.



Keep posting progress. Seeing people react is the best motivation there is.
